reason: The attribution holds up, but the proposed change does not. (A) ATTRIBUTION CONFIRMED. The est formula is right: 0.95/128,883 = 1/135,666, about 1/D with D = TP+FP+FN = 135,729. So each dropped FP is worth +0.9/D, each lost TP -1/D, and the break-even drop precision is 1/1.9 = 0.526. On all 199 videos with the absolute 3.5 um pre-linefit flag plus post-freeze, ef comes to about +0.0136: drops (0.9*1,890 - 234)/D = +0.0108 and re-links (495 TP - 0.9*152 FP)/D = +0.0026. Ordinary transitions give only +0.00064 of it (4.7%). (B) THE PROPOSED ef_anom FAILS ITS OWN SUCCESS CRITERION. The hypothesis proposes a RELATIVE 1.8x flag. With that flag the unflagged 'normal' class still carries +0.0030 of 0.0136 (22%) on all videos, 17% on confirmation, and up to 44-53% with the ILP-tight median or 2.2x. Drop precision there is 0.78-0.86, far above the 0.526 break-even. So ef_anom would give up about -0.002 to -0.007 locally to 'protect' a class whose measured contribution is POSITIVE (+0.0006). The absolute 3.5 um flag keeps about 95%, so it equals ef within 0.0006; the LB cannot resolve that (3-decimal rounding is +-0.0005), and a probe or final slot spent on it has zero expected value. Either way, change (1) brings no gain. (C) THE FINALS-POLICY ARITHMETIC IS WRONG IN ITS KEY STEP. The research says a '44b6-like' embryo would gain only about +0.0015. That uses the global denominator. Normalised within the embryo (D_44b6 about 21k from the parquet: 18,763 TP, 1,322 FP), the 44b6 anomalous class alone is 243 edge-units, i.e. +0.0115, plus +0.0006 for normal transitions. The replay measured 44b6 at +0.0145 and 6bba at +0.0169. So an embryo that flags only 6% of its transitions and has no frozen frames (44b6) still gains more than +0.012. The gain density is about +0.002 per 1% of anomalous transitions, because those transitions carry base FP rates of 0.24-0.34. A flat probe 29 (+-0.002) therefore needs a public embryo with under ~1% anomalous transitions, which matches neither training embryo, OR a failure to transfer the in-sample ILP evidence. The second is the likelier reading. Then the private embryos would fail the same way, and the claimed conditional private upside (0.3-0.6 x 0.0146 = +0.004..0.009) is optimistic by roughly 2-4x. (D) Branch (c)'s claim that '<= -0.003 cannot come from ordinary transitions' holds for a 6bba-like annotation density. The worst case there is -(195 drops + 0.9*112 re-links)/114k = -0.0026, realistic about -0.001. For a sparse 44b6-like embryo it is only marginal: worst case -0.0066, realistic about -0.002. (E) There is no public gain toward 0.97 in any branch. The public number is whatever probe 29 reports.
fix_if_any: Drop change (1): do not build ef_anom with any relative flag, since it loses 17-53% of ef's local gain. The absolute flag equals ef, so it is pointless as a variant. Keep the finals policy only as a costless hedge, with corrected arithmetic. Two finals are allowed and the better private score counts, so pairing '<best base> + ef' with '<best base>' when S29 is flat costs one slot's opportunity and nothing else. But read a flat S29 as 'probably no transfer', not 'public embryo lacks anomalies'. Break the tie with probe 30 (drop-only ef_a0, which does not rely on in-sample ILP choices). If S30 >= +0.003 while S29 is flat, the in-sample re-link is the problem: ship the drop-only filter in one final. If both are flat, put the second final on coordhead/stitch rather than ef, because a transfer failure would hit the private embryos equally. Optionally, one CPU replay can log a label-free per-video anomalous-transition rate (frozen = >80% zero-length edges; big-step = pre-linefit ILP median >3.5 um) in the kernel on the hidden test clips, printed to stdout only. The kernel log on hidden data is not visible either, so this check verifies only the code path.
realistic_public_gain: 0.000 directly: ef_anom equals ef (absolute flag) or does worse than it (relative flag, -0.002 to -0.007 locally). Public ef gain is whatever probe 29 shows. If ef transfers, both train embryos imply about +0.012-0.015 per embryo, with ~95% from anomalous transitions. Conditional on a flat public probe, the private value of keeping ef in one final is about +0.001-0.003 (not +0.004-0.009), because a flat result most likely means non-transfer.
